newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Black still mulls Fairfax Strype issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Black still mulls Fairfax Strype issue.

text.p: Canadian media baron Conrad Black said on Wednesday his media group Hollinger International Inc was still planning a Strypes or related options issue of its 25 percent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
"It may not be a Strype, it might be something closely related," Black told reporters after Fairfax's annual meeting.

"The reasoning behind that (Strype) would be at least we would have some ultilization of most of the cash value of the investment," Black said. "We would have a three year window with which to use the cash and at the end of the three years to either come back into the stock or have the cash," he said.

Under a Strype (structured yield product exchangable for common stock) issue, Black would continue to hold the Fairfax shares and receive dividends with an option to repurchase the Strypes in three years.
Hollinger is controlled by Black and holds the Fairfax stake through its U.K. subsidiary, the Telegraph Plc.
Black is currently prevented from increasing his 25 percent stake by government rules on foreign ownership of the media, but the Coaltion government is holding a study into media ownership.
Hollinger's stake in Fairfax is valued at about A$500 million based on current market prices.
At 1.20 p.m. (0220 GMT), Fairfax shares were one cent up at A$2.68.
